name: python-frontend-open-points
body:
Design points for the Python frontend. All previously-deferred points are now DECIDED; none remains open.

(1) Module FQN namespace form — DECIDED (language rooting, Human decision folded into the scanner-optimisation change-set): the rendered Python Module FQN is the language-rooted form `py.<dotted-identity>`. Python package identity is the init-bearing dotted name; under the language root `py` it is disjoint from every other language's module namespace (a root package `apg` renders `py.apg`, distinct from Rust's `rust.apg`) and from markdown's rooted absolute paths, so cross-language collision-freedom and collision-freedom for package-qualified dotted identities hold by construction. The root does NOT make flat init-less modules globally unique: a flat module's identity is its stem alone, so `a/foo.py` and `b/foo.py` both render `py.foo` and the second is silently shadowed — flat modules are unique only within their directory (requirements.requirement.python-package-identity).

(2) Cython / .pyx — pinned OUT of the accepted set (requirements.requirement.python-accept-extensions) because `ty` cannot parse Cython exactly; whether a future Cython frontend or a tree-sitter heuristic arm is wanted is a later user call, not this change-set's concern.

(3) uv/venv project-context model — DECIDED (Human): the frontend auto-detects the project environment — a uv project (pyproject.toml/uv.lock), a virtualenv, or a bare src root — and supplies it to `ty`'s project context, so third-party imports resolve against the real environment. `site-packages`/a virtualenv stays a discovery exclusion (never a scan root, emits no code nodes; domain.constraint.python-exclusions) and is available ONLY as a resolution input in the full `ty` project context (global.constraint.frontend-full-context). The auto-detection is the frontend's own environment discovery, not a new APG config surface.

(4) Ruff/ty pin currency — DECIDED (policy): `astral-sh/ruff` is pinned to a release tag as git deps (the reference used 0.16.6) and bumped ATOMICALLY — all ty/ruff crates move together and the lockfile is re-pinned in one change — exactly as src/rustlib does for rust-analyzer. The exact tag is confirmed at implementation time (the reference's 0.16.6 is validated against current main's needs when the frontend is built); the atomic-bump policy is the durable decision, the tag number is not (requirements.constraint.python-ty-ruff-pin-policy).

(5) Incremental target-set granularity — DECIDED (Human): Python's granularity is per-package/module (aligned with the package identity model and `ty`'s module-level analysis). The interface: the frontend receives a target set of modules/packages; resolution still runs against the full `ty` project (imports and base classes cross files), and only emission is filtered to the target set. This feeds requirements.requirement.python-incremental-contract and requirements.requirement.full-context-targeted-emission.
